capabilities: Publish plugin lifecycle, context menu, file, canvas, task, command, workspace, configuration, sync and mobile keyboard events on app.workspace
Provide typed API declarations (api.d.ts) that developers can copy or consume via a cross-plugin registry
Ship a demo vault with live-subscription notes explaining each event
Expose a versioned API contract with schemas for arguments and return values
disambiguation: It has no user interface; it is an API surface for other plugins, not an end-user tool.
extras: Documentation is itself a demo vault shipped with each release and browsable on GitHub; no similar plugin was found when last searched, on 2026-10-26.
intentEvidence: A home for the events Obsidian does not publish. More Events publishes them on app.workspace, named, typed and per subject
motivation: Without it, a plugin that needs such an event reads undocumented internals or patches a shared prototype, and two plugins doing that in one vault means two patches on one prototype. This plugin patches once, for everybody.
problem: Plugins that need events Obsidian does not publish must read undocumented internals or patch a shared prototype, which conflicts when several plugins do it.

relations.evidence: Ensure you have the BRAT plugin installed and enabled.

summary: Developer library that publishes named, typed workspace events Obsidian's public API does not expose, letting plugins subscribe without patching internals.
